1.why: Every MFA endpoint resolves the user solely from the server-side session map via authorized(), and any body containing userId/accountId/ownerId is rejected by invalidIdentifierAttempt().

2.why: OTPs are derived from a per-user AES-GCM-encrypted provisioning secret and recovery codes are hashed per-user, so a code from one account cannot verify another (only one demo account exists, and no cross-user path exists).

3.why: verify-authenticator sets mfaActive without deleting or rotating the existing session id (rotation occurs only at /api/login), so pre-existing sessions remain valid after MFA is enabled.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored as AES-GCM ciphertext+IV via encryptSecret(), and backup codes are stored only as SHA-256 digests with a random process pepper.

5.why: Master key, pepper, session/CSRF tokens, provisioning secrets and recovery codes all come from crypto.getRandomValues().

6.why: No localStorage/sessionStorage is used and both mfa_session and mfa_preauth cookies are HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict, though CSRF tokens and secrets do live transiently in JS memory.

7.why: Server-side regex/length validators (validEmail, validPhone, validOtp, validSecret, validRecovery, normalizedLoginEmail) gate every endpoint, and there is no SQL/database layer.

8.why: All dynamic values (secret, recovery codes, error messages) are inserted with textContent; innerHTML is used only with static literal markup.

9.why: safeInternalPath() enforces a fixed allow-list of internal hash routes and defaults to #/dashboard, and no server-issued Location redirects exist; the returned 'next' is not actually consumed by the client.

10.why: standardHeaders() sets HSTS, CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy and no-store, though the CSP weakens itself with script-src 'unsafe-inline'.

11.why: sessionCookie()/preAuthCookie() both emit HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict with Path and Max-Age.

12.why: Errors are generic with no stack traces and nothing sensitive is in URLs, but /api/provision returns manualSecret and testOtp and the client mockLog() writes the authenticator secret, current OTP and all recovery codes to the console and an on-page log panel.

13.why: TOTP acceptance is limited to the current 30s step with a usedSteps replay set, provisioning expires after 15 minutes, and matched recovery codes are spliced out of the stored list.

14.why: recordFailure()/failureBlocked() lock login (hashed-email keyed), authenticator verification and recovery verification for 10 minutes after 5 failures, plus a 60s throttle on backup-code regeneration.

15.why: Login deletes any old session id and issues a fresh random one, sessions enforce a 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute expiry, and logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
